Philippines' Largest Crypto Exchange Coins ph Halts Transfers to and from Self-Custody Wallets Coins ph, the Philippines’ largest cryptocurrency exchange, announced that effective November 19, it no longer supports direct crypto deposits or withdrawals involving self-custody wallets. Users may only transfer assets to or from accounts at other regulated exchanges. Under the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) Travel Rule requirements, all external transfers, regardless of amount, require counterparty details, wallet type, exchange platform, and transaction purpose. Incoming deposits will be credited only after the required information is verified. — link

Highlight Clip: CleanSpark CBO: Power Access Will Be Bitcoin Miners' Key Competitive Advantage CleanSpark CBO: Power Access Will Be Bitcoin Miners' Key Competitive Advantage CleanSpark CBO Harry Sudock told What Bitcoin Did on November 5 that if starting a company today, he'd build an energy business first, then decide whether its power would serve Bitcoin mining or AI. CleanSpark measures its business in megawatt-hours, megawatts, and acres, with AI data centers offering a way to realize their value. Bitcoin miners can adjust electricity consumption based on prices or contracts, while AI data centers manage grid balancing differently. Sudock sees transmission, not generation, as the main US power-grid bottleneck, requiring further investment in transmission and distribution alongside solar, natural gas, and nuclear power. — link

Vitalik Criticizes Racial Stereotypes in Netflix's Portrayal of CZ, Questions Whether It Is Racist Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin criticized Netflix's portrayal of Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) in a production involving FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF) and Caroline Ellison. Buterin said CZ's accent had been made to sound roughly three times more foreign than he remembered. He also criticized the production for reinforcing the stereotype that people travel to foreign countries only to engage in suspicious activities. Buterin questioned whether such a portrayal should be called "racist," suggesting that society may have moved far enough beyond "woke" culture for the term to be used again. — link
